reviews.title: annotation import rejects deeply nested JSON before migration or replacement
reviews.primaryContract: Deeply nested Annotation JSON is rejected by the bounded JSON parser before migration or document replacement, without changing Canonical revision.
reviews.reason: The shared parser unit contract does not prove this file-input route invokes depth validation before Annotation migration; Signal Event Import has a separate parser adapter and remains independently covered.

reviews.title: Signal Event Import rejects deeply nested JSON before values are replaced
reviews.primaryContract: Deeply nested Signal Event JSON is rejected before replacing the selected Signal's values, leaving revision and History unchanged.
reviews.reason: Signal Event Import previously bypassed the shared parse gate, so its adapter-specific ordering and no-replacement guarantee are distinct from Annotation import's depth check.

reviews.title: Signal Event Import rejects an oversized file before it is read as JSON
reviews.primaryContract: A file larger than the configured byte budget is rejected before JSON parsing and leaves Canonical revision and History unchanged.
reviews.reason: Nesting-depth validation does not cover byte-size preflight; this uses an actual oversized file on disk because inline Playwright buffers have a 50MB cap, protecting the pre-read boundary itself.

reviews.title: Advanced JSON rejects a resource overflow before document replacement
reviews.primaryContract: Applying Advanced JSON with a cycle-count resource overflow reports validation failure before replacing the current document and leaves revision, History, Dirty, and session intact.
reviews.reason: Advanced JSON is a separate whole-document replacement adapter and validates timeline cycle budget, unlike entity/file import routes; it specifically protects against replacing the active session on invalid JSON semantics.

reviews.title: does not select an annotation rejected by import
reviews.primaryContract: When Annotation import is rejected, the failed attempted Annotation is not selected and the previous selection remains unchanged.
reviews.reason: The resource-limit suite protects document atomicity but this case isolates the success-only selection side effect after a rejected import; failed commands must not move transient selection to a nonexistent entity.

reviews.title: does not select a transaction when creation is rejected
reviews.primaryContract: When Transaction creation is rejected, no synthetic/nonexistent Transaction ID becomes selected and the prior selection remains unchanged.
reviews.reason: Annotation import rejection covers a different create adapter/entity; this directly guards the Transaction create route's result-aware selection effect, which resource-budget tests alone do not assert.

reviews.title: Review Refresh Checks is view-only
reviews.primaryContract: Refreshing Review checks leaves Canonical revision, History, Dirty state, and render counters unchanged.
reviews.reason: The review workflow filtering case proves filter/navigation are view-only after checks exist, but does not guard the explicit refresh action from mutating the document or triggering render work.

reviews.title: Problems exposes Clear Filter for filter clearing
reviews.primaryContract: Problems panel presents the Clear Filter affordance and no stale Refresh control in its current panel header.
reviews.reason: This is a narrow panel-header/accessible-control migration guard: the full Review workflow case covers scope and severity filters but does not assert the Problems table's Clear Filter control or absence of the obsolete Refresh action. It verifies the affordance, not the clearing interaction itself.

reviews.title: Review filters and navigates the shared Problems diagnostics without mutation
reviews.primaryContract: Review scope/severity filters and Previous/Next navigation operate on shared diagnostics while preserving Canonical revision, History, and Dirty state.
reviews.reason: This is the end-to-end diagnostics workflow across a real invalid edit, multiple scope/severity filter states, and navigation targets; refresh-only and layout-only tests cover separate boundaries and do not imply the workflow semantics.

reviews.title: Check header separates Filter/Navigation/Summary/Status/Action into non-overlapping groups (#394)
reviews.primaryContract: The five Check header groups remain in the intended order, share aligned control baselines, and do not overlap at the tested production viewport.
reviews.reason: The behavioral Review workflow tests do not protect the #394 density regression where controls collide; this directly checks grouping, order, overlap, and alignment rather than duplicating filter behavior.

reviews.title: Ribbon caption layout survives mode changes at 1280
reviews.primaryContract: At 1280x720, changing Cycle/Transaction/Combined modes preserves Ribbon height and keeps each visible group caption below its body without pseudo-element duplication.
reviews.reason: This compact viewport detects caption collision/wrapping changes during mode transitions that static Ribbon label tests do not measure; its paired wide case covers a distinct responsive width.

reviews.title: Ribbon caption layout survives mode changes at 1672
reviews.primaryContract: At 1672x941, changing Cycle/Transaction/Combined modes preserves Ribbon height and keeps each visible group caption below its body without pseudo-element duplication.
reviews.reason: The reference-width counterpart checks group caption geometry over the same mode lifecycle; compact-width wrapping behavior cannot establish desktop alignment.

reviews.title: Cursor A/B Ribbon controls set/swap/clear the status bar readout with zero Canonical/History delta
reviews.primaryContract: View Ribbon controls set, move, swap, and clear source-time cursor A/B state, update guide/status projections, and remain view-only with zero History mutation.
reviews.reason: This exercises the full Ribbon-to-workspace cursor lifecycle and status projection; geometry-only cursor tests do not cover set/swap/clear command wiring or no-History behavior.

reviews.title: Cursor A guide drag updates only workspace cursor state
reviews.primaryContract: Dragging Cursor A to a semantic Cycle boundary updates its source-time position while leaving Canonical and History unchanged.
reviews.reason: The set/swap/clear case does not exercise pointer coordinate projection or guide drag; this separately protects the cursor-only drag mutation boundary.

reviews.title: Home Ribbon labels and icons do not overlap at 1365px
reviews.primaryContract: At 1365px, visible Home Ribbon icons and labels remain within their buttons and Timeline controls do not overlap neighboring controls, with no horizontal Ribbon overflow.
reviews.reason: This intermediate-width overlap check targets icon/label and sibling-control geometry, not text wrapping alone; the 1672px case is its wide responsive counterpart and existing wrapping tests assert a different text contract.

reviews.title: Home Ribbon labels and icons do not overlap at 1672px
reviews.primaryContract: At 1672px, visible Home Ribbon icons and labels remain within their buttons and Timeline controls do not overlap neighboring controls, with no horizontal Ribbon overflow.
reviews.reason: This verifies icon-label and Timeline sibling geometry at the approved wide reference width; the narrower viewport can fail independently, and word-boundary wrapping checks do not detect these collisions.

reviews.title: does not create horizontal Ribbon overflow at 1024px
reviews.primaryContract: At 1024px, the Home Ribbon's scroll width does not exceed its client width.
reviews.reason: The 1024px responsive-overflow case already asserts the same no-scrollbar width invariant and additionally opens More to verify command reachability; retaining this standalone assertion duplicates that breakpoint.

reviews.title: does not create horizontal Ribbon overflow at 1280px

reviews.primaryContract: At 1672px, the Home Ribbon's scroll width does not exceed its client width.

reviews.primaryContract: At 1024px, More popup stays inside viewport, supports arrow/Home/End focus navigation, closes on Escape or tab switch, restores focus, and causes no document mutation.

reviews.title: keeps More popup inside the viewport and view-only at 900px
reviews.primaryContract: At 900px, More popup stays inside viewport, supports arrow/Home/End focus navigation, closes on Escape or tab switch, restores focus, and causes no document mutation.
reviews.reason: This verifies the popup at the narrowest tested viewport where positioning and available menu space differ from 1024px; the command inventory test does not assert overlay bounds or keyboard dismissal lifecycle.

reviews.title: keeps Home commands reachable without a Ribbon scrollbar at 1024px
reviews.primaryContract: At 1024px, Home Ribbon has no horizontal scrollbar, relocates commands into More, exposes the required command set, and allows view-only Select All through that menu.
reviews.reason: This is the compact-width command reachability contract and also absorbs the duplicate 1024px overflow-only assertion; no desktop grouping or standalone popup-bound test proves the relocated command inventory.

reviews.title: keeps Home commands reachable without a Ribbon scrollbar at 1280px
reviews.primaryContract: At 1280px, Home Ribbon remains scrollbar-free and exposes the documented major-group order; compact mode retains this contract while moving commands to More.
reviews.reason: The 1280px boundary validates the full ribbon group composition while the paired 1024px case checks relocation/reachability; it also subsumes the standalone overflow-only assertion at the same width.

reviews.title: Home overflow zoom presets remain view-only at compact width
reviews.primaryContract: A zoom preset selected from the compact Home More menu changes view zoom while leaving Canonical revision, History, and Dirty state unchanged.
reviews.reason: Menu reachability alone does not establish that a relocated zoom action uses the view-only route rather than mutating document/history state; this is a focused adapter contract.

reviews.title: Home Ribbon swaps Time/Layout for Transaction context on ViewMode change, with exact Undo/Redo and no canonical/history/dirty delta from the switch itself
reviews.primaryContract: Switching between Cycle and Transaction changes the Home Ribbon group composition and Bottom context without mutating Canonical/History/Dirty; Transaction creation remains one Undo/Redo-able command.
reviews.reason: Static responsive tests do not validate ViewMode-owned group projection or Bottom context synchronization, and the create/Undo/Redo portion protects the retained Transaction action route.

reviews.title: Home Ribbon has no overlap/clipping in Transaction context at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: At 1280x720 in Transaction context, the Home Ribbon scroll width does not exceed the client width.
reviews.reason: The generic narrow Ribbon check runs without explicitly switching to Transaction context; this checks the different Transaction-context group set at the compact supported viewport.

reviews.title: Home Ribbon has no overlap/clipping in Transaction context at 1672x941
reviews.primaryContract: At 1672x941 in Transaction context, the Home Ribbon scroll width does not exceed the client width.
reviews.reason: The wide reference check verifies overflow under Transaction-specific Home composition; Cycle/wide label geometry tests do not switch to this context or assert its client/scroll width relationship.

reviews.title: captures deterministic production Ribbon scenario manifests
reviews.primaryContract: At the reference viewport, each Ribbon tab produces a deterministic scenario manifest with icon/baseline diagnostics, capture metadata, and no console/page/resource failures.
reviews.reason: This is the only all-tab production capture/manifest integrity sweep and validates the review-bundle evidence format as well as each tab's icon/baseline diagnostics; individual layout checks do not verify manifest completeness or runtime failures across all tabs.

reviews.title: covers compressed Ribbon layout and Home round-trip without semantic mutation
reviews.primaryContract: At 1365x800, Ribbon tab round-trips preserve Ribbon height/workspace position and document state, remain scrollbar-free, and yield clean compressed/round-trip icon-baseline manifests.
reviews.reason: The desktop all-tab capture does not exercise the intermediate compressed viewport or repeated Home round-trip stability; this is a visual evidence scenario rather than routine semantic coverage.

reviews.title: keeps the Ruler alive across edits, Undo/Redo, and repeated Opens with a non-default reference clock
reviews.primaryContract: Ruler geometry remains present and correctly changes across Signal/event edits, Undo/Redo, and repeated opens of two documents with distinct non-default Reference Clock IDs and cycle counts.
reviews.reason: Reference label persistence does not cover stale ruler/geometry ownership across successive document generations; this lifecycle specifically switches A→B→A and checks each document's tick projection after edits and history replay.

reviews.title: derives the reference Clock label and edge from canonical state across Save/Open
reviews.primaryContract: Selecting a different stable Reference Clock, changing its edge and name, and Save/Open derives the Time Axis status/context labels and serialized clock/edge from Canonical state.
reviews.reason: The A→B→A ruler test only checks tick availability/count; this separately proves user-visible stable clock identity, edge, rename propagation, and persisted Time Axis ownership.

reviews.title: the Ruler resolves and renders the terminal timeline boundary tick instead of silently omitting it
reviews.primaryContract: For a half-open timeline [0, cycleCount), the Ruler resolves and renders the terminal cycleCount boundary at an X greater than the preceding tick.
reviews.reason: Ordinary tick-count and reference-clock tests do not assert the final exclusive-end boundary, which may be represented only as the previous cycle's end geometry.

reviews.title: Open then Annotation drag uses the current document geometry
reviews.primaryContract: After opening a document, an Inspector-selected stable Annotation ID is used to drag its endpoint against the newly opened document's current Cycle geometry and snap to the intended cycle.
reviews.reason: General Annotation drag tests do not exercise the Open→render-owner replacement→drag sequence; the target is now selected by Inspector's canonical Annotation ID rather than DOM order, preserving stable identity under overlay reuse.

reviews.title: resize then edit then zoom reads current ViewMetrics and keeps semantics coherent
reviews.primaryContract: After resizing Inspector, an immediate Signal edit and subsequent zoom use current ViewMetrics while preserving semantic selection/data and a mounted waveform.
reviews.reason: The ordered resize→edit→zoom sequence catches stale layout metrics consumed by a later command; isolated resize and zoom cases cannot establish that consumers switch to the current metrics between operations.

reviews.title: Signal Editor's in-progress Add/Edit Transition draft survives an unrelated canonical edit
reviews.primaryContract: An uncommitted Bottom Signal event draft survives an unrelated canonical visibility edit to another Signal, retains the original editor selection, and is still explicitly cancelable.
reviews.reason: Local field editing/Cancel tests do not protect against whole-document revision remount erasing the draft when another entity changes; this reproduces that cross-entity lifecycle directly.

reviews.title: moves the selected Signal to a Group via the dropdown + Move button, using the real signal.move command
reviews.primaryContract: Bottom's Group dropdown plus Move button invokes one reversible signal.move command, disables same-group no-op, and updates the selected Signal's current-group projection.
reviews.reason: The sibling test covers moving into an empty Group; this covers the populated destination and same-group disabled guard through the dedicated Bottom editor adapter, preserving semantic role and Undo behavior.

reviews.title: Inspector Signal Properties Apply stays disabled until the Draft actually differs from the committed Signal
reviews.primaryContract: Inspector Apply is disabled for an unchanged Signal draft, becomes enabled after a role change without immediate Canonical mutation, then applies one update and disables again.
reviews.reason: The broader Name/Role test validates independent commit paths, but this directly protects the Draft dirty-state gate and disabled/enabled transition that prevents accidental no-op Apply commands.

reviews.title: Inspector applies per-signal vertical spacing through the canonical command
reviews.primaryContract: Inspector spacing fields commit via the canonical Signal command, change the next row's rendered vertical position, avoid WaveDrom regeneration, and are Undoable.
reviews.reason: This covers a layout-affecting Signal property and its actual row-geometry effect; role/name/type tests protect different property-specific rendering and command semantics.

reviews.title: follows row selection and exposes derived Event Table columns
reviews.primaryContract: The Bottom Signal editor follows the selected stable Signal and exposes its derived event rows with stable read-only Start/Value/End/Duration fields and quick-value actions.
reviews.reason: Mutation tests assume an already selected Signal and do not assert selection-to-editor projection or the table's derived read-only columns; this is the base user entry/structure contract.

reviews.title: commits one event edit once, rerenders only its waveform, and supports Undo
reviews.primaryContract: Editing and saving one event changes that Signal's waveform exactly once, preserves unrelated waveform SVG identity and row positions, and Undo restores prior event semantics.
reviews.reason: The simpler event-row tests establish editing UX but do not assert owner-local WaveDrom/geometry invalidation or that an unrelated waveform is retained; this is the direct incremental-render boundary.

reviews.title: Inspector Name (Enter) and Role (Apply) each commit independently without WaveDrom regeneration
reviews.primaryContract: Inspector name commits on Enter and role commits through Apply as two distinct one-revision actions, with the rendered row updated and WaveDrom untouched.
reviews.reason: Apply gating covers only role-draft enablement and type/width covers a different command payload; this protects the separate InlineNameInput Enter commit and the intended independent Name/Role ownership paths.

reviews.title: Inspector exposes editable type and bus width through one semantic command
reviews.primaryContract: Inspector applies Signal type/role and Bus width together as one semantic command, and Undo restores the canonical width.
reviews.reason: Bus width is type-specific canonical data and is not exercised by generic Name/Role/Spacing property cases; this verifies a single atomic type/width update and undo restoration.

reviews.title: Bottom Signal event toolbar provides command-backed row operations, and the table footer provides export
reviews.primaryContract: Bottom event toolbar exposes only Duplicate/Add Row/Delete, event export is available in the table footer, and Duplicate commits one additional row in one History unit.
reviews.reason: This protects the post-#402 toolbar/footer ownership and a real row-duplicate command; import/undo, transition editing, and table selection are tested separately and do not assert the relocated export affordance.

reviews.title: Bottom Signal event Import (table footer) replaces the table in one history entry and Undo restores it
reviews.primaryContract: Importing an event table from the footer replaces the selected Signal's values in one History operation and Undo restores the prior table.
reviews.reason: Resource-boundary tests protect rejected oversized/deep files, not successful replacement semantics, exact one-command history, or Undo restoration of the prior event table.

reviews.title: edits Clock Generator through one semantic history entry
reviews.primaryContract: Applying a Clock period edit produces one semantic History operation, regenerates only the Clock waveform/geometry owner once, and reflects the committed period in the editor.
reviews.reason: Duty/suppressed-period cases cover specialized generator values; this is the base period-edit command and incremental owner invalidation contract.

reviews.title: Bottom Clock editor applies exact non-50% Duty through WaveDrom and preserves Undo/Redo
reviews.primaryContract: A 25% Clock duty edit changes the rendered WaveDrom use geometry, rebuilds only the clock owner once, and restores/reapplies through Undo/Redo and Save/Open.
reviews.reason: Period editing does not validate non-50% duty rendering; this checks waveform geometry change, one-owner invalidation, history replay, and persisted duty semantics.

reviews.title: Bottom Clock editor applies suppressed periods and preserves them through Save/Open
reviews.primaryContract: Duplicate suppressed periods are rejected without History, valid distinct suppressed periods update the Clock waveform, and the accepted list survives Undo/Redo and Save/Open.
reviews.reason: Duty/period tests do not cover suppression-list validation or phase omissions; this is the dedicated invalid/valid list boundary and persistence path.

reviews.title: Bottom Clock editor exposes Edge Counter settings through its own semantic command
reviews.primaryContract: Bottom Clock editor applies edge-counter visibility, edge mode, and count origin as one semantic operation, renders numbering without rebuilding WaveDrom/geometry, and Undo restores the disabled state.
reviews.reason: Edge Counter is independent presentation metadata and has its own editor command; clock generator output edits do not verify numbering mode/count origin or overlay-only invalidation.

reviews.title: Bottom Clock context toolbar exposes real preset, duplicate, import, export and preview actions
reviews.primaryContract: The selected Clock context toolbar presents Presets/Duplicate/Import/Export/Preview, preview is view-only, the 50%-duty preset is actionable, and Duplicate creates/selects one Clock.
reviews.reason: This protects the Clock-specific action surface and exercises preview/preset/duplicate behavior; Import and Export are asserted as available buttons here, not as completed file-I/O workflows, so dedicated file lifecycle tests remain necessary.

reviews.title: moves the rendered waveform transition to the edited Start cycle, not just the DOM identity
reviews.primaryContract: After editing an event Start cycle, the actual rendered transition geometry moves to the corresponding Ruler boundary while remaining absent from the old boundary.
reviews.reason: Canonical row-value assertions cannot establish that the WaveDrom transition moved to the new semantic cycle; this is the rendered geometry acceptance for Start editing.

reviews.title: #402: Event row Save stays disabled until the Draft differs, and Cancel discards it back to canonical
reviews.primaryContract: Read-only event rows expose no edit controls until Edit, unchanged Draft keeps Save disabled, changed Draft marks unapplied state, Cancel restores Canonical without History, and Save commits one operation.
reviews.reason: Immediate Add semantics and unrelated-edit draft survival cover different workflows; this directly protects the row-local Edit→dirty draft→Cancel/Save lifecycle and avoids invisible idle inputs.

reviews.title: Transitions table Select All is a real tri-state checkbox wired to the same selection the footer bulk actions use
reviews.primaryContract: The transition table Select All checkbox correctly reflects unchecked/indeterminate/checked states, shares selection with per-row checkboxes and footer count, and honors bulk-action cardinality guards.
reviews.reason: Transition reorder tests use selected rows but do not verify tri-state checkbox semantics, accessible row labels, selection count synchronization, or Delete/Move enablement constraints.

reviews.title: Transition drag handle reorders rows through one history entry
reviews.primaryContract: Dragging an individual transition handle changes event-row order through one semantic History operation and the updated row values are projected in order.
reviews.reason: Selected block Move Up/Down actions are distinct toolbar command paths; neither protects the row drag-handle adapter and its one-operation commit.

reviews.title: Selected transition block moves down as one semantic unit
reviews.primaryContract: Moving a contiguous selected transition block down preserves block selection and performs one semantic reorder without creating or deleting rows.
reviews.reason: This tests the direction-specific selected-block boundary and selection tracking; the up/Undo case covers the opposite edge and history replay, while drag reorder exercises another adapter.

reviews.title: Selected transition block moves up and restores through Undo/Redo
reviews.primaryContract: Moving a selected transition block upward changes its order once and Undo/Redo restores/reapplies the order while retaining the complete row set.
reviews.reason: The selected-block down case does not cover upward boundary behavior or history replay; a drag-handle single-row move is not a substitute for selected contiguous-block movement.

reviews.title: Signal event table explains its immediate-commit model and Add still produces one History entry
reviews.primaryContract: The event form clearly communicates immediate per-Add commit semantics and adding an event creates exactly one History step.
reviews.reason: The event Save/Cancel case covers deferred row-edit drafts, not the distinct immediate Add/Add & Continue interaction model; this pairs truthful guidance with its one-step behavior.

reviews.title: shows an inset clear affordance only for non-empty signal filters
reviews.primaryContract: The Signal Tree clear button appears only for non-empty input, is inset and vertically aligned within the search field, and clears the filter back to its absent state.
reviews.reason: Filtering behavior tests do not protect the conditional clear affordance's containment/alignment or its empty-state disappearance; this is a compact UI geometry plus interaction contract.

reviews.title: edits individual signal spacing through Inspector with local row invalidation and Save/Open
reviews.primaryContract: Applying per-Signal spacing moves subsequent rows, updates row positions without WaveDrom/local-geometry rebuild, supports Undo/Redo, and survives Save/Open.
reviews.reason: The base spacing case in signal-editor.spec.ts only checks a row displacement and Undo; this adds precise row-position-only invalidation plus persisted reconstruction for a Signal-specific spacing value.

reviews.title: keeps invalid Group and Signal spacing drafts out of the canonical document
reviews.primaryContract: Negative Group and Signal spacing drafts are rejected without Canonical revision, History, or Dirty changes.
reviews.reason: Valid spacing persistence does not exercise invalid numeric values across both Group and Signal owners; this guards rejected drafts from leaking into Canonical state or creating History.

reviews.title: edits Group and Signal spacing independently and together with exact persistence and export
reviews.primaryContract: Group before/after spacing, Signal before/after spacing, and document layout spacing apply as separate commands, serialize exactly, restore through Save/Open, and remain represented in SVG/PNG/PDF exports.
reviews.reason: This combines three distinct spacing owners and verifies exact file serialization plus all three export formats; local Signal spacing Save/Open alone cannot prove Group/global spacing ownership or export projection.

reviews.primaryContract: Cycle Inspector does not expose the retired per-Signal Upper/Lower/Both Split Pane assignment control.
reviews.reason: The existing Sample D dual-viewport acceptance already selects a Signal and asserts the retired Split Pane Inspector control is absent while exercising the canonical shared-row product model; this default-document absence-only check adds no distinct fixture or state transition.

reviews.title: Signal Split shows the same canonical Signal sequence in both panes
reviews.primaryContract: Both Split panes project the same first five canonical timing-row IDs in the default Cycle fixture.

reviews.title: toggling Signal Split is view-only and Upper's own scroll position survives toggling Lower off and back on
reviews.primaryContract: Toggling the Lower viewport is view-only and preserves Upper's horizontal scroll position across OFF/ON while the shared ruler remains synchronized.

reviews.title: Upper and Lower scroll vertically independently while sharing one horizontal time domain

reviews.title: Signal types stay synchronized through history and Save/Open at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: The supported Signal type labels remain identical between creation and Inspector controls, and type changes survive Undo/Redo and Save/Open at 1280x720.
reviews.reason: The compact viewport exercises the type-registry and persisted role contract under narrower responsive layout; the wide viewport cannot replace this breakpoint-sensitive check.

reviews.title: Signal types stay synchronized through history and Save/Open at 1672x941
reviews.primaryContract: The supported Signal type labels remain identical between creation and Inspector controls, and type changes survive Undo/Redo and Save/Open at 1672x941.
reviews.reason: This proves the type-registry and serialized-role lifecycle at the wide acceptance viewport; the compact case independently protects the smaller layout.

reviews.title: hiding a signal keeps its navigation row recoverable while removing its waveform row
reviews.primaryContract: Hiding a Signal retains its navigation identity while removing it from timing/frozen/wave projections, and restoring it returns the same canonical Signal to aligned surfaces.
reviews.reason: Stable SVG reuse tests cover renderer identity and Inspector tests cover row alignment; this protects the distinct user recovery path where a hidden item remains discoverable in the Tree and can be restored.

reviews.title: creates a Spacer from the Insert Ribbon, duplicates/copies it, reorders it within its Group by drag, and rejects a cross-Group drop
reviews.primaryContract: Insert, Duplicate, clipboard copy/paste, same-Group drag reorder, and cross-Group rejection preserve Spacer height/identity and semantic command/history rules.
reviews.reason: This uniquely covers the Insert Ribbon adapter, fresh identity on copy, in-Group drag, and Core's cross-Group Spacer rejection; Tree Add and Group Inspector edit tests do not cover these operations.

reviews.title: adds and edits a Spacer Row from the Group Inspector with Save/Open and Undo/Redo
reviews.primaryContract: Group Inspector Spacer height drafts reject invalid values without commit, valid Apply commits one reversible edit, and height survives Save/Open and exports.
reviews.reason: Tree Add covers creation and projection only; this covers Group Inspector height editing, invalid draft isolation, Apply, history, persistence, and export reconstruction.

reviews.title: creates a first-class Spacer from the Tree Add surface
reviews.primaryContract: Tree Add creates a canonical Spacer with one History entry and projects a row without rebuilding WaveDrom or local timing geometry.
reviews.reason: Insert Ribbon and Group Inspector routes use different production adapters; this directly guards Tree Add selection, row projection, and the Spacer no-wave/no-geometry invalidation contract.

reviews.title: Split active pane follows clicks on the Signal surface vs Transaction lanes, drives ActiveContext, and stays view-only
reviews.primaryContract: In Combined mode, Signal-surface and Transaction-lane interactions update active-pane/ActiveContext ownership without Canonical or History mutation.
reviews.reason: Sibling drag tests verify specific gesture routes; this covers general click/focus ownership, context-sensitive Ribbon change, and view-only behavior across both active panes.

reviews.title: Cycle and Transaction restore their last valid Bottom tab independently
reviews.primaryContract: Switching between Cycle and Transaction restores each mode's last valid Bottom tab without leaking the other mode's selection.
reviews.reason: This is the only test of per-mode Bottom-tab memory and validates fallback to each mode's valid tab instead of a shared global selection.

reviews.title: Combined routes a real Transaction bar drag to the Transaction pane only
reviews.primaryContract: A real Transaction bar drag in Combined mode mutates the Transaction through its owner, leaves Cycle editor idle, and activates the Transaction pane.
reviews.reason: This real-pointer Transaction gesture asserts one semantic edit, Cycle editor isolation, and active-pane ownership; Signal range selection and mode-switch tests do not replace it.

reviews.title: Transaction to Combined and back preserves Transaction ownership
reviews.primaryContract: Transaction remains the active owner on entering Combined and its bars remain present after returning to Transaction, with no new History entry.
reviews.reason: Active-pane interaction does not cover mode transition restoration; this checks Transaction→Combined→Transaction ownership and view-only History preservation.

reviews.title: Combined routes a Signal waveform range drag to the Signal pane only
reviews.primaryContract: A real waveform range drag in Combined resolves source cycles from Cycle ruler geometry, routes selection to the Signal pane, and creates no Canonical/History change.
reviews.reason: Transaction drag protects the opposite owner route; this specifically verifies Signal range coordinates/source cycles and view-only selection in Combined.

reviews.title: low-level view mode pointerdown cancels a Transaction drag before pointerup
reviews.primaryContract: A low-level mode switch during an active Transaction drag cancels the preview before pointerup and prevents a stale semantic edit from committing.
reviews.reason: Completed drag and mode round-trip tests do not exercise cancellation during an in-flight pointer sequence; this guards against stale gesture ownership committing after workspace change.

reviews.title: never generates a colliding Stable ID after a page reload resets the in-memory counter
reviews.primaryContract: After Save/Open in a fresh module session resets the in-memory ID counter, newly created Signals still receive IDs unique across the document.
reviews.reason: Stable IDs are canonical identity rather than position; this exercises actual restore and subsequent authoring that can expose counter collisions beyond pure generator unit tests.

reviews.title: reorders row shells without rerendering or moving heavy WaveDrom SVG owners
reviews.primaryContract: Row-shell reorder and viewport remount preserve heavy WaveDrom SVG owner identity/order while only updating row positions and keeping canonical/rendered row mappings aligned.
reviews.reason: This deterministic Phase 5 surface probe measures expensive SVG owner identity and render counters across viewport remount/reorder; product-level reorder tests do not enforce renderer reuse.
